content.thinking:
I'm writing up the postmortem: the metrics stopped because a port name rename in values-production.yaml stopped matching the ServiceMonitor's selector, while the shop kept serving normally, with the same ClientDisconnected rate in the logs and the account page rendering fine. Nobody using the service noticed anything wrong. Now I'm comparing the log request counts from before and after the gap.

I'm checking whether the logs really look like normal service, since the error rate roughly doubled (0.5% to 1.0%) while the range stayed the same at 0.50%-1.50%, and the highest value matches the earlier peak. I'm leaning toward calling it serving as before, because the errors are shopper-caused ClientDisconnected ones and nothing failed or slowed.

I'm working out the causal chain now: the shoppers noticed nothing, but the shop's metrics stopped being collected. The likely reason is that the scraper no longer finds its target, since the port rename broke the name match. I'm not yet sure the scrape config still selects the old name, because the only evidence for that is a reading I haven't actually run.

I'm checking whether the claim that the scrape config still selects "metrics" holds up, since only one unrun reading supports it, though the rollback result points the same way. Next I'm tracing why the name stopped matching: the deploy changed the port name from "metrics" to "http-metrics", and it reached all replicas by 03:21.

I'm ruling out the earlier deploy: metrics were still being collected after it went out and before the onset, and rolling back to that revision brought them back. I'm also checking that no flag changes happened, apart from the automated ones.

I'm working out why the deploy broke it: the scrape config picks its target by port name, so once the name changed, the scraper found nothing to collect from.

I'm laying out the causal chain for the postmortem: shoppers saw nothing wrong, but the shop's metrics stopped being collected. Next I'm tracing why, starting with the deploy that renamed the metrics port and reached every replica by 03:21:22. The last step is why that rename broke collection: the scrape config picks its target by port name and still asks for the old one, so the scraper found nothing to collect from.

I'm settling on the root cause: the scrape config picks the shop's metrics target by port name, and the deploy renamed that port from "metrics" to "http-metrics" without updating the name the scrape config selects, so nothing matched and the scraper had nothing to collect.

I'm weighing whether the fix could backfire: the rename might go out again, or the repository's version could be synced back in before the scrape config matches, which would stop metrics collection a second time. Nothing currently catches a mismatch like that before it ships.

I'm weighing whether the next deploy could bring the same problem back: if the port rename goes out again, or the scrape configuration is updated to the new name in a way that doesn't line up with what's running, metrics would stop again without anything flagging the mismatch first.

I'm weighing how to frame the fix: a check that the port name in the values file matches the name the scrape configuration selects, since nothing caught the mismatch before the change went out.

I'm weighing whether the monitoring alert should have caught this sooner: it fired only on missing series, and nobody was paged, though Argus handled it within a minute. I'm not yet sure that paging gap belongs among the contributing factors.

I'm settling on which contributing factors belong in the postmortem: the alert firing only on missing series with nobody paged is a went-wrong item, and the late alert, with about 3m33s unaccounted for, could be a separate factor worth tracing.

I'm turning to the scaleDownStabilizationSeconds setting that the diff shows, and checking whether it has anything to do with the monitoring gap.

I'm now drafting the action items: a CI check that fails any change where a ServiceMonitor endpoint's port name matches nothing the deployment renders, applied to every service and not just io-shop. A second item is finding out what delayed the alert by the unexplained gap, and a third is deciding whether the MetricsAbsent alert on io-shop should page on-call.

Now I'm noting what went well: the investigator agent read the diff and pinned the port rename at T12, the mitigation agent rolled back at T19 and confirmed metrics were readable again by T22, and the code-fix agent proposed draft pull request #546 at T24. I'm also dating the onset back to T6 for the timeline.

Now I'm weighing what went wrong beyond the missing check: the monitoring alert fired only on missing series and paged nobody, so I'm noting that as its own finding for the postmortem. I'm not adding any lucky breaks, since the record doesn't show any chance factor, and I'm leaving the luck section empty. Last, I'm checking the assumptions: the customer-loss comparison uses the same hours from earlier weeks, and the claim that the running scrape config selects "metrics" comes from a reading I haven't verified.

I'm checking the assumptions: the ClientDisconnected errors and account-page warnings are compared against the minutes before the gap, and the replicas are taken to have run the revision read at T13. Then I'm writing the first step of the causal chain, that nobody using the shop saw anything wrong while its metrics stopped being collected after the minute at T5.2.

Now I'm weighing the second step of the chain: the deploy of revision 9f4ad14 renamed the metrics port in the production values file, and every replica was running it by then.

I'm checking the two ruled-out candidates: the earlier deploy e283ba3 is out because metrics were still being collected with it in place up to 03:20, and they became readable again once the rollback restored it. The flag changes are out too, since the hour before shows no changes by anyone other than Argus.

I'm checking whether the port-number detail matters for the postmortem, and deciding it doesn't. I'm also weighing the two contributing factors: a pre-deploy check would have caught the mismatch before production, and a faster alert would have shortened the stretch the shop went unwatched.

action_items.item: Add a pre-deploy CI check, applied to every service and not only io-shop, that fails any change where a scrape endpoint's port name matches none of the port names the deployment renders.
Find what delayed the MetricsAbsent alert on io-shop by {beyond_accounted_for} beyond what its evaluation accounts for, and remove that delay.
Link MetricsAbsent on io-shop to the on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: No sign was seen that anyone using the shop had a problem. What was seen instead was that the shop's metrics stopped arriving, and no samples covered the minutes after they stopped.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision e283ba3af732fc4285166a060b827b1305cd30d9 at {P1.1}. Metrics were collected with it in place up to the minute at {T5.2}. Once the rollback put that revision back, the metrics could be read again.
A feature-flag change. The flag provider's history shows {T16.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus in the hour before {T16.4}.

causal_chain.step: The deploy of revision 9f4ad14582c99c497eb6c2d2af87566cd4493020 at {P2.1} changed one value in deploy/values-production.yaml: it renamed the metrics port from metrics to http-metrics and left the port number at {D1.1}. When read at {T13.1}, all {T13.2} replicas were running that revision.
The scrape configuration picks the shop's metrics target by the port's name and was still looking for metrics, so after the rename it matched no port and had nothing to collect.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A configuration change renamed the label the monitoring system uses to find the shop's figures, and the monitoring setup most likely still looked for the old name, so it stopped collecting them.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that would catch the port name in deploy/values-production.yaml no longer matching the name the scrape configuration selects. The values file's own comment says nothing in the shop reads that name, and that a name nothing matches fails silently. A rename in one file could therefore ship without the other file changing.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The mismatch would have been caught before the deploy reached production, and the shop's metrics would not have stopped.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The MetricsAbsent alert fired {beyond_accounted_for} later than its evaluation interval, the scraping allowance and the minute-level dating of the stop can explain. The record does not show what took the extra time.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The alert would have fired sooner, and the stretch when the shop's metrics went unwatched would have been shorter.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent read the deploy's diff, which pinned the change down to the renamed metrics port.
The Mitigation Agent rolled back the deployment of io-shop off the renamed port.
The Mitigation Agent saw that the metrics could be read again and confirmed that the rollback had worked.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request #546.

went_wrong: When MetricsAbsent fired on io-shop, nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to it.

input.root_cause: The scrape configuration finds the shop's metrics target by the port's name, not its number, and the deploy renamed that port in deploy/values-production.yaml from metrics to http-metrics without changing the name deploy/scrape.yaml selects, which is still metrics. The selector then matched no port, and the scraper had nothing left to collect.
input.still_at_risk: Any deploy that names the metrics port differently from the name the scrape configuration looks for, whether the same rename going out again or one of the two files changing without the other, would quietly stop the shop's metrics being collected again without raising any error.
input.symptom: Shoppers saw nothing wrong, but the shop's metrics stopped being collected
